text:
pagerbot: PAGER: kv-cache fragmentation + continuous-batching latency spike detected in inference-serving-prod. metric=kv_fragmentation_ratio rising rapidly, 95th token latency > 800ms for cu-rt-eu-1. alert_id=PD-9834. paging oncall

maya (SRE): I'm oncall, jumping in. starting log collection now. which customer(s) reporting errors?

customer-success: seeing timeouts from ingestion pipeline for two customers (acme-analytics, simon-llm). they're seeing 5xxs on batch ingest and slow completions. escalated at 13:07 UTC.

liam (Runtime Eng): looking at allocator metrics — arena free lists are fragmented, small slab churn spike since 13:02. continuous-batching config shows an increase in avg batch length due to a recent model rollout. suspect KV prefix churn -> heap fragmentation -> cudaMalloc pressure.

maya (SRE): can you paste the noisy logs / top OOM msgs?

liam (Runtime Eng): logs: ```
[13:05:12] kv_arena: alloc_size=8192, slab_id=47, free_frag_pct=72.4
[13:05:13] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[13:05:13] pytorch: failed to allocate tensor (13:05:13) size=1.2GB
[13:06:02] kv_batch: avg_batch_tokens=1024, max_inflight=120
```

seb (ML Infra): this matches a behavior we saw in pre-prod last month — large prefix variance leads to many different KV cache entries, small allocations dominate and cause slab starvation. arena compaction didn't kick in because compaction threshold was tuned low to avoid CPU spikes.

olivia (Oncall): immediate mitigation options? throttle batching? enable compaction? pin fallback to smaller model?

liam (Runtime Eng): lowest-risk fast mitigation: reduce continuous-batching max tokens & max batch size for cu-rt-eu-1 and route heavy requests to warm-backed variant. Proposed changes: `kv_batch.max_tokens: 1024 -> 256`, `kv_batch.max_batch: 120 -> 32`. Will also enable aggressive arena compaction flag `kv_arena.compact_on_free=true` as an experiment for the cluster.

maya (SRE): go for config change first. make it a canary on 2 nodes, watch 1m metric window, then roll. apply throttles and patch routing. keep customer-success updated.

liam (Runtime Eng): applying canary now (kubectl patch svc inference-cu-rt-eu-1 --patch ...). command: ```
kubectl apply -f /ops/k8s/canary/kv-batch-throttle-cu-rt-eu-1.yaml
```

infra-bot: rollout started for kv-batch-throttle-cu-rt-eu-1 canary (2/24 pods). health checks passing.

maya (SRE): seeing immediate drop in 95th latency to ~220ms on canary nodes. fragmentation ratio trending down from 72% -> 48% on canary.

customer-success: acme-analytics reports retries succeeding after ~1m. Simon-LLM still seeing intermittent failures but rate reduced.

liam (Runtime Eng): enabling `kv_arena.compact_on_free=true` on canary now. small risk: CPU spike while compaction runs. watching CPU and p99 latency.

infra-bot: kv_arena.compact_on_free enabled on canary nodes. CPU increased +3%, p95 stable.

maya (SRE): can we also temporarily disable continuous-batching for streaming endpoints? That drops throughput but reduces churn.

liam (Runtime Eng): disabling continuous-batching for streaming on the cluster — applied. ```
# disable flag
redis-cli SET config:streaming:continuous_batching 0
```

seb (ML Infra): long-term: need arena resizing + slab coalescing change in allocator. I'll open a follow-up PR to add an adaptive compaction threshold based on observed free_frag_pct and cudaMalloc failures. Reference: PR #4126.

olivia (Oncall): customer impact: moderate for 2 customers for ~20 minutes, mitigated to low after canary. Ops note: route fallback to smaller model increased token cost by ~8% during mitigation window. Logging all actions for postmortem.

maya (SRE): preparing summary for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = increased prefix diversity from recent model rollout + change in batching patterns -> many small KV allocations -> slab fragmentation -> cudaMalloc pressure. Immediate mitigations: throttle batch sizes, enable compaction, disable continuous-batching for streaming, route heavy customers to smaller model. Long-term: allocator tuning (coalesce small frees), automated compaction triggers, add telemetry for fragmentation early-warning.

eng-runtime: PR for hotfix config created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/5678 (kv-batch emergency throttle). will green-roll to all nodes after 30m stable window.

infra-bot: canary stable for 22m, rolling to remaining nodes (24/24 pods).

customer-success: both customers confirmed resolution. closing CCs.

maya (SRE): logging final numbers: total requests failed ~0.9% of window, 95th latency peak 820ms -> baseline 180ms after rollout. No data exfiltration or correctness issues. tagging for postmortem. handing to night oncall @olivia for follow-up and postmortem writeup. :thumbsup:

olivia (Oncall): acknowledged, will own postmortem. leaving note to include cost delta and PR refs. handing off.

pagerbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: PD-9834 closed at 13:42 UTC.
